title: Grade 4 SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — General Assessment #13

pages.quiz:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #13
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Nitrogen gas only
   B. Only water vapour
   C. Only carbon dioxide
   D. Glucose and oxygen

2. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Burning crop residue every week
   B. Removing all vegetation
   C. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   D. Overgrazing continuously

3. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Paper burning to ash
   B. Ice melting to water
   C. Milk souring
   D. Iron rusting

4. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Properties of Matter? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Properties of Matter.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Properties of Matter.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Properties of Matter.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Properties of Matter.

5. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. A mixture of two liquids
   B. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   C. Any white crystal used in cooking
   D. Any substance that conducts electricity

6. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water removes heat too quickly
   B. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   C. Petrol fires have no fuel
   D. Water always increases oxygen

7. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 100 °C
   B. 50 °C
   C. 0 °C
   D. 37 °C

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Light? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Light.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Light.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Light.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Light.

9. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. watt (W)
   B. pascal (Pa)
   C. newton (N)
   D. joule (J)

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Water Conservation? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Water Conservation.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Water Conservation.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Water Conservation.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Water Conservation.

11. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   B. A chemical reaction forming ash
   C. Movement of water only across a membrane
   D. Heating until a solid melts

12. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   B. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   C. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   D. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Heat and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Properties of Matter and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Water Conservation and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Light and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. D — Glucose and oxygen

2. C — Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

3. B — Ice melting to water

4. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Properties of Matter.

5. B — A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

6. B — Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

7. A — 100 °C

8. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Light.

9. C — newton (N)

10. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Water Conservation.

11. A — Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

12. D — Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Water Conservation; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
